all.altText:
Türkiye’s crypto asset sector is on the threshold of a new era. Ahead of the authorization process, the debate is no longer only about which platforms will continue operating, but also about how competition will take shape after licensing, how banks will position themselves in the sector, and how crypto platforms will evolve.

To view this new era from a global perspective, we sat down with Bybit CEO Ben Zhou. Zhou, who places Türkiye among the world’s top five crypto markets, believes that after licensing, local players will focus more on product capabilities while global platforms will place greater emphasis on localization. With Zhou, who expects cooperation rather than competition to define the relationship between banks and crypto platforms, we discussed the new era spanning Bybit’s ambitions in Türkiye, stablecoins, artificial intelligence and security.

$BTC There has been quite a bit of open interest ramp up over the past two days.

Well over $1.3B on Bitcoin alone has entered.

Presumably the majority is longs that have built up into the price that has grinded up. Most are obviously sitting comfy but that last leg in open interest saw a lot enter in the $85.5-$86K region.

Bulls need to keep it above that area to not risk a reversal and squeeze of those (late) longs. But the coinbase discount has slowly been going down so that means there's some spot bid coming back slowly the past day or two.

We have NFP coming up in a little under 5 hours. With yields high and inflation fears still going, a lot of investors will be looking at this number. Especially at the start of a new quarter, this is bound to cause volatility.

tweets.text:
The best traders are very fluid

You could have had an idea yesterday, thats no longer valid today or whatever time frame. But ultimately, you aren't married to any idea or position. Whether you are trading eth, or wheat futures. All that matters is your pnl. They are really just tickers to trade with changing narratives, rotations, and liquidity. Sometimes people get on a trend late and still make more than someone who was early. People are wrong all the time, but the best learn to correct it quick and admit that. More often than not marrying a ticker comes with many big costs whether emotional, or financially. 

All that matters is what you make, and keep, and that we get paid for the risk we take. See so many people crap on people who had an idea one week, and then the opposite week their opinion changed as new information came in. That's exactly how you are suppose to be. fluid
